questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which term describes the maximum population size an environment can sustain indefinitely?
questions.hint: It is shown by the plateau of an S-shaped curve.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: In a sigmoid (logistic) growth curve, the transitional phase begins when:
options: limiting factors start to slow the growth rate
the population first colonises the habitat
questions.answer: limiting factors start to slow the growth rate
questions.hint: Resources become less available as numbers rise.

questions.q: Capture–mark–release–recapture: 40 beetles are marked and released. Later, 50 are caught, of which 8 are marked. Estimate the population size using the Lincoln index.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Only about 10% of energy is typically transferred between trophic levels mainly because:
options: energy is lost as heat from cell respiration and in undigested material
energy is destroyed at each level
consumers store all energy as fat
questions.answer: energy is lost as heat from cell respiration and in undigested material
questions.hint: Energy is not created or destroyed, but it leaves the food chain.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A species that has a disproportionately large effect on community structure relative to its abundance is a:
questions.hint: Removing it can cause the community to collapse, like an arch without its key stone.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which statement about natural selection is correct?
options: Individuals with heritable traits that increase survival and reproduction pass on alleles more often.
Individuals change their genes to adapt during their lifetime.
Acquired characteristics are inherited by offspring.
Selection creates new mutations when they are needed.
questions.answer: Individuals with heritable traits that increase survival and reproduction pass on alleles more often.
questions.hint: Variation must already exist and be heritable.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What type of speciation occurs when a population is divided by a geographical barrier?
questions.hint: 'Allo' means 'other'; 'patric' refers to the homeland.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Abrupt speciation in plants often occurs through:
options: geographical isolation over millions of years
questions.hint: Changes in the number of chromosome sets can isolate a new population instantly.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Differences in mating behaviour that prevent two populations from interbreeding are an example of:
questions.hint: The barrier acts before fertilisation.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A clade is best defined as:
options: a common ancestor and all of its descendants
all species in the same habitat
a group of species that cannot interbreed
questions.answer: a common ancestor and all of its descendants
questions.hint: Think of one branch of a cladogram, cut off completely.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: The three domains of life are:
questions.hint: Classification based mainly on rRNA sequences.

questions.subject: bio

questions.hint: First calculate p = 1 − q.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Calculate Simpson's reciprocal index (D = N(N−1) ÷ Σn(n−1)) for a sample with three species of 4, 3 and 3 individuals. Give your answer to 2 decimal places.
questions.hint: N = 10. Calculate n(n−1) for each species and add them.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Outline how antibiotic resistance in bacteria provides evidence for evolution by natural selection.
questions.hint: Include variation, selection pressure, survival and reproduction, and change in allele frequency.

questions.subject: bio

questions.hint: Think about food supply, competition and overshoot.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Discuss two reasons why biodiversity is currently declining and evaluate one conservation strategy (in situ or ex situ).
questions.hint: Use command terms: give strengths and limitations of the strategy.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A group of organisms of the same species living in the same area at the same time is a:

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which factor is density-dependent?
questions.hint: Its effect becomes stronger as the population grows.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Capture–mark–release–recapture: 30 snails are marked and released. Later, 40 are caught, of which 6 are marked. Estimate the population size using the Lincoln index.

questions.subject: bio

questions.hint: They form the first trophic level.

questions.subject: bio

questions.hint: Apply 10% twice.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which statement about mutualism is correct?
options: Both species benefit from the interaction.
One species benefits and the other is harmed.
One species benefits and the other is unaffected.
questions.answer: Both species benefit from the interaction.
questions.hint: Think of pollinators and flowering plants.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which is the best example of evidence for evolution?
options: homologous structures such as the pentadactyl limb
questions.answer: homologous structures such as the pentadactyl limb
questions.hint: Similar structures suggest common ancestry.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: For natural selection to occur, there must be:
questions.hint: Selection acts on differences that can be inherited.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What is the term for the formation of a new species?
questions.hint: It often follows reproductive isolation.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: In binomial nomenclature, the first part of a scientific name is the:
questions.hint: It is written with a capital letter.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which group is a domain of life?
questions.hint: There are three domains in total.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Cladograms are increasingly based on:
questions.hint: Molecular data act like a clock of change.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Higher biodiversity in an ecosystem is generally associated with:
questions.hint: More species can buffer disturbances.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Outline how antibiotic resistance in bacteria develops by natural selection.
questions.hint: Variation, selection by the antibiotic, survival and reproduction.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Explain why a population that grows exponentially cannot keep doing so indefinitely.
questions.hint: Think of limiting factors and carrying capacity.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Suggest two human activities that reduce biodiversity and one way to reduce the impact of each.
questions.hint: For example, habitat loss and overexploitation.

hold large buffer stocks for emergencies
buy raw materials in bulk once a year
questions.answer: minimise stock holding by receiving supplies only when needed

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What is the Japanese term for continuous small improvements in production?

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Quality assurance differs from quality control because it:

removes the need for any standards

questions.hint: A strong recommendation weighs both sides before concluding.

questions.subject: bus

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Evaluate the use of a Boston matrix for a firm deciding which products to invest in.
questions.hint: Mention its usefulness and at least two limitations.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: How many Ps are in the traditional marketing mix for goods?
questions.hint: Product, price, promotion and…

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which element of the marketing mix refers to how a product reaches customers?
questions.hint: Also called distribution.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Setting a high initial price for an innovative product is called:
questions.hint: Like removing the cream from the top of milk.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Pricing a product at $9.99 instead of $10 is an example of:
questions.hint: It plays on how customers perceive numbers.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: In the product life cycle, sales grow most rapidly during the:

questions.answer: a 'buy one get one free' offer in store

questions.subject: bus

large amounts of stock are always kept
stock is ordered once a year
goods are made before customers order them

questions.hint: It reduces storage costs.

questions.q: Price per unit is $20, variable cost per unit is $12 and fixed costs are $24,000. Calculate the break-even quantity.

questions.subject: bus

questions.hint: Consider cost, reach and the target market.

questions.subject: bus

chem-sl.topic: Review: organic chemistry and reaction mechanisms

questions.q: What was the 1933 law that allowed Hitler to make laws without the Reichstag?
questions.hint: It 'enabled' him to rule by decree.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Which structure works best for a paragraph in an IB History essay?
options: point, evidence, analysis, link to the question
questions.answer: point, evidence, analysis, link to the question
questions.hint: Each paragraph should argue, not just describe.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Evaluate the importance of the Cuban Missile Crisis in changing superpower relations. (3–5 sentences)
questions.hint: Think about the hotline, the Test Ban Treaty and the path to détente.

questions.subject: hist
questions.q: Examine the role of propaganda in maintaining one authoritarian state of your choice. (3–5 sentences)
questions.hint: Consider the cult of personality, censorship and education.

math-hl.topic: Review: integration, differential equations and series

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the exact value of ∫ from 0 to 1 of 3x² dx.
questions.hint: Integrate, then substitute the limits.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find ∫ e^(2x) dx.
questions.hint: Differentiate each option to check.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Using integration by parts, find ∫ x e^x dx.
questions.hint: Let u = x and dv = e^x dx.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the exact value of ∫ from 0 to π/2 of cos x dx.
questions.hint: An antiderivative of cos x is sin x.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find ∫ 1/(1 + x²) dx.
questions.hint: Which function has derivative 1/(1 + x²)?

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find ∫ 2x/(x² + 1) dx.
questions.hint: Notice the numerator is the derivative of the denominator.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find ∫ ln x dx.
questions.hint: Use parts with u = ln x and dv = 1 dx.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: What are the first three terms of the Maclaurin series for e^x?
questions.hint: Every derivative of e^x at 0 equals 1.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the coefficient of x³ in the Maclaurin series of sin x. Give your answer as a fraction.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Using Maclaurin series, find the limit of (1 − cos x)/x² as x → 0. Give your answer as a fraction.
questions.hint: cos x ≈ 1 − x²/2 for small x.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: What is the general solution of dy/dx = ky, where k is a constant?
questions.hint: Separate the variables and integrate.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Solve dy/dx = 2y with y(0) = 3. Find the value of y when x = ln 2.
questions.hint: y = 3e^(2x); simplify e^(2 ln 2).

questions.subject: math
questions.q: What is the integrating factor for dy/dx + (2/x)y = x, x > 0?
questions.hint: Compute e^(∫ 2/x dx).

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Use Euler's method with step size h = 0.1 to estimate y(0.1) for dy/dx = x + y, y(0) = 1.
questions.hint: y₁ = y₀ + h·f(x₀, y₀).

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the area enclosed between y = x and y = x² for 0 ≤ x ≤ 1. Give your answer as a fraction.
questions.hint: Integrate (upper curve − lower curve).

questions.subject: math
questions.q: The region under y = √x from x = 0 to x = 4 is rotated 360° about the x-axis. The volume is kπ. Find k.
questions.hint: V = π∫ y² dx.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Given f(x) = 3x⁴, find f'(2).
questions.hint: Differentiate first: bring the power down and reduce it by 1.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the derivative of sin(3x).
questions.hint: Use the chain rule.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the derivative of x e^x.
questions.hint: Use the product rule.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the gradient of the tangent to y = x² + 3x at x = 1.
questions.hint: Differentiate, then substitute x = 1.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the x-coordinate of the stationary point of y = x² − 6x + 1.
questions.hint: Set dy/dx = 0.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: At a stationary point, f''(x) > 0. What type of point is it?
options: it cannot be a stationary point
questions.hint: Positive second derivative means the curve is concave up.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the value of ∫ from 1 to 3 of 2x dx.
questions.hint: An antiderivative of 2x is x².

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find ∫ cos x dx.
questions.hint: Which function has derivative cos x?

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the area under y = 3x² between x = 0 and x = 2.
questions.hint: Integrate 3x² from 0 to 2.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: A particle has velocity v(t) = 3t² − 12 m/s. Find its acceleration at t = 2 s.
questions.hint: Acceleration is the derivative of velocity.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: A particle has displacement s(t) = t³ − 6t² metres. Find the time t > 0 when the particle is at rest.
questions.hint: At rest means v = ds/dt = 0.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: A particle has velocity v(t) = 2t + 1 m/s, which is always positive for t ≥ 0. Find the distance travelled from t = 0 to t = 3 s.
questions.hint: Integrate v(t) over the interval.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the derivative of ln x.
questions.hint: Defined for x > 0.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Given y = (2x + 1)³, find dy/dx at x = 0.
questions.hint: Chain rule: 3(2x + 1)² × 2.

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Find the derivative of e^(x²).
questions.hint: Chain rule with inner function x².

questions.subject: math
questions.q: Explain how the second derivative can be used to decide whether a stationary point is a maximum or a minimum.
questions.hint: Think about what f''(x) tells you about concavity.

phys-hl.topic: Review: nuclear, quantum and stellar physics

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Which particles are emitted in beta-minus decay?
questions.hint: A neutron changes into a proton.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A radioactive isotope has a half-life of 5 days. What fraction of the original nuclei remains after 15 days? Give a fraction.
questions.hint: How many half-lives is 15 days?

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: What does an alpha particle consist of?
questions.hint: It is identical to a helium-4 nucleus.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: What process provides the energy of main-sequence stars?
questions.hint: Light nuclei join together in the core.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: What happens in the core of a main-sequence star?
questions.hint: The most abundant element is the fuel.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Calculate the energy of a photon of frequency 5.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz (h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s). Give your answer in units of 10⁻¹⁹ J to 2 s.f.
questions.hint: Use E = hf.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: In the photoelectric effect, what does increasing the light intensity (above the threshold frequency) increase?
options: the number of photoelectrons emitted per second
the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons
questions.answer: the number of photoelectrons emitted per second
questions.hint: More photons, but each with the same energy.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: According to Wien's displacement law, a hotter star has its peak emission at…
questions.hint: λmax × T is constant.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A star has a surface temperature of 5800 K. Using λmax T = 2.9 × 10⁻³ m K, find λmax in nm to 2 s.f.
questions.hint: Divide, then convert metres to nanometres.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Which nucleus has approximately the highest binding energy per nucleon?
questions.hint: It sits at the peak of the curve.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Where are white dwarfs found on the Hertzsprung–Russell diagram?
questions.hint: Hot but faint.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: What is the very dense stellar remnant made mainly of neutrons, left after some supernovae?
questions.hint: It is smaller than a city but more massive than the Sun.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A nuclear reaction has a mass defect of 0.0300 u. Using 1 u = 931.5 MeV c⁻², find the energy released in MeV to 3 s.f.
questions.hint: Multiply the mass defect by 931.5.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: If a star's surface temperature doubles while its radius stays the same, its luminosity becomes…
questions.hint: L = σAT⁴.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: If the momentum of an electron doubles, its de Broglie wavelength…
questions.hint: λ = h/p.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Explain why nuclear fusion in stars requires extremely high temperatures. (3–5 sentences)
questions.hint: Think about the electrostatic repulsion between nuclei.

phys-sl.topic: Review: nuclear, quantum and stellar physics

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: What do isotopes of the same element have in common?
questions.hint: The proton number defines the element.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: An isotope has a half-life of 3 hours. What fraction remains after 12 hours? Give a fraction.
questions.hint: Count the half-lives in 12 hours.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Which type of radiation is the most penetrating?
questions.hint: It has no charge and no mass.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: In beta-minus decay, an electron is emitted together with which other particle?
questions.hint: Lepton number must be conserved.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Uranium-238 undergoes alpha decay. What is the nucleon number of the daughter nucleus?
questions.hint: An alpha particle carries away 4 nucleons.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: What happens in nuclear fission?
options: a heavy nucleus splits into smaller nuclei
questions.answer: a heavy nucleus splits into smaller nuclei
questions.hint: It is used in nuclear power stations.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: What is the SI unit of activity of a radioactive source?
questions.hint: One decay per second.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: In the photoelectric effect, what is the threshold frequency?
options: the minimum frequency needed to emit electrons
the frequency at which electrons stop moving
the highest frequency of visible light
questions.answer: the minimum frequency needed to emit electrons
questions.hint: Below it, no electrons are emitted however bright the light.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A metal has a work function of 2.0 eV. Light with photons of energy 3.5 eV hits it. Find the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons in eV.
questions.hint: Photon energy = work function + maximum kinetic energy.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: What is the luminosity of a star?
questions.hint: Measured in watts.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: What keeps a main-sequence star in equilibrium?
options: gravity balanced by radiation and gas pressure
questions.answer: gravity balanced by radiation and gas pressure
questions.hint: Inward pull versus outward push.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: What will a star like the Sun eventually become after its red giant phase?
questions.hint: It is small, hot and dim.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: A star's distance from Earth doubles. By what factor does its apparent brightness change? Give a fraction.
questions.hint: b = L / (4πd²).

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: When does a star like the Sun begin its red giant phase?
options: when hydrogen in its core runs out
when iron forms in its core
when it becomes a neutron star
questions.answer: when hydrogen in its core runs out
questions.hint: The core contracts and the outer layers expand.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Which quantities are conserved in a nuclear equation?
questions.hint: Check the top and bottom numbers on both sides.

questions.subject: phys
questions.q: Explain how the binding energy per nucleon curve shows that both fission and fusion can release energy.
questions.hint: Think about which direction moves nuclei towards iron-56.
